subject: BridgeOps connector compatibility validation request
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@bridgeops.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Tim Sato <tim@langchain.dev>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@promptway.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: BridgeOps Connector v1.3 — compatibility validation request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the runway at Redwood Connect. We’re preparing the BridgeOps Connector v1.3 release and would like Redwood to run a lightweight compatibility validation so we can call out certification in our release notes. Key areas we’re worried about:

- KV/prefix cache handling for long-lived sessions (we surface partial KV state across reconnects)
- Token attribution/usage reporting when calls are proxied through an adapter
- Function-call / tool-invocation mapping (we map tool outputs to a standard JSON envelope)

We’ve attached the connector_spec_v1.3.pdf that shows the integration surface and a short matrix of expected behaviors. Ideally we’d get a confirmation that the connector works with Redwood’s hosted runtime and any blockers surfaced in a short validation report.

As context: we will provide a sandbox API key and sample request vectors — if you need a private mirror image of your runtime for staging tests we can stand that up for a short window.

Asks:
1) Can Redwood run an initial pass (smoke + telemetry check) and send back a short validation note?
2) If you need more time, what would a minimal test plan look like from your side and who should we loop in at Redwood?

If helpful, Tim at LangChain offered to run some adapter-level traces as well (CC’d).

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick 30-min call.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Integrations, BridgeOps
elena@bridgeops.ai
Attachment: connector_spec_v1.3.pdf (application/pdf, 380KB)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@bridgeops.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeOps Connector v1.3 — compatibility validation request

Elena —

Thanks for the detail and the spec. We can absolutely run a targeted compatibility validation. Proposed plan:

1) Initial smoke and telemetry pass (48–72 hours): basic end-to-end requests, trace capture for token attribution, and a quick KV reconnect test.
2) Extended validation (up to 7 business days): stress two long-session scenarios, rune through function-call mapping against our function-calling shim, and verify consumption reporting.
3) Deliverables: a one-page validation note listing blockers and a follow-up checklist for certification.

What we need from you to start:
- Temporary sandbox API key (read/write) or short-lived staging cluster credentials
- A set of ~20 sample vectors (happy path + 4 edge cases)
- A short reference for your function-envelope schema (example payloads)

I’ve CC’d Vanessa to own infra/test execution and Jonas to own telemetry/tracing and the function-call agreement. Vanessa — can you provision a mod sandbox under /sandboxes/bridgeops-v1 once we have credentials? Jonas — can you list the minimal trace hooks you need (we’ll try to map to your example payloads)?

We can aim to have the initial pass complete by Friday if you can share the sandbox/key today. If not, we’ll slot it for next week.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-9211

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BridgeOps Connector v1.3 — compatibility validation request

Forwarding BridgeOps’ ask — please see Elena’s spec (attached). High level tasks and owners below:

Vanessa: provision staging sandbox under /sandboxes/bridgeops-v1, run infra health checks, execute the integration_qa_checklist.csv, and exercise reconnect/kv scenarios. Attach redwood_infra_test_plan.yaml to the sandbox.

Jonas: capture traces for token attribution and function-call mapping. Please provide a short text file with the trace hooks you want us to emit so BridgeOps can correlate on their side.

Timeline: initial smoke (48–72h) after we get credentials. Deliver a one-page validation note and list of blockers. If we see anything that requires an API shim on Redwood side we’ll highlight as an action item for the platform team.

Kimberly / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I’ve attached the sample vectors (bridgeops_sample_vectors.json) and created a sandbox key for you: RBW-bridgeops-staging-2025 (expires 2025-06-20). I’ve also left a short note in the Drive folder with expected pass criteria. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-bridgeops-connector-spec

We’ll schedule a 30-min sync on Monday to review initial findings — I’ll drop a calendar invite.

If anything looks like a blocker (e.g., non-deterministic token attribution when proxied) let me know and we’ll prioritize a quick patch on our adapter.

Appreciate the help —
Elena
Attachment: bridgeops_sample_vectors.json (application/json, 14KB)
